q: A particle moves along a line with displacement s = 2t³ − 5t + 1 metres at time t seconds. Its velocity at t = 2 s is:
x: v = ds/dt = 6t² − 5, so v(2) = 24 − 5 = 19 m/s. 7 is s(2), the displacement, not the velocity.

q: A particle has displacement s = 2t³ − 15t² + 36t (t ≥ 0). It is momentarily at rest when:
x: v = 6t² − 30t + 36 = 6(t − 2)(t − 3), which is zero at t = 2 and t = 3. Check t = 2: 24 − 60 + 36 = 0. t = 5/2 is where the acceleration 12t − 30 is zero.

q: The velocity of a particle is v = 4t² − 3t m/s. Its acceleration at t = 1 s is:
x: a = dv/dt = 8t − 3, so a(1) = 5 m/s². 1 is the velocity v(1), not the acceleration.

q: A particle has acceleration a = 6t − 4 m/s² and its velocity at t = 0 is 3 m/s. Its velocity at t = 2 s is:
x: v = ∫(6t − 4) dt = 3t² − 4t + c, and v(0) = 3 gives c = 3. So v(2) = 12 − 8 + 3 = 7 m/s. Leaving out the constant gives 4; 8 is a(2).

q: A particle starts from the origin with velocity v = 3t² + 2t m/s. Its displacement from the origin at t = 2 s is:
x: s = ∫(3t² + 2t) dt = t³ + t² + c, and s(0) = 0 gives c = 0. So s(2) = 8 + 4 = 12 m. 16 is v(2).

q: A particle moves with velocity v = t − 2 m/s. The total distance it travels from t = 0 to t = 4 s is:
x: v < 0 on [0, 2) and v > 0 on (2, 4]. ∫₀² (t − 2) dt = −2 and ∫₂⁴ (t − 2) dt = 2, so the distance is 2 + 2 = 4 m. Integrating straight across gives the displacement 0, not the distance.

q: A particle moves with velocity v = 2t − 6 m/s. Its displacement from t = 0 to t = 4 s is:
x: ∫₀⁴ (2t − 6) dt = [t² − 6t]₀⁴ = 16 − 24 = −8 m. 10 m is the total distance (9 m back, then 1 m forward), not the displacement.

q: A ball is thrown upward and its height is s = 40t − 5t² metres after t seconds. Its greatest height is:
x: v = 40 − 10t = 0 at t = 4 s, and s(4) = 160 − 80 = 80 m. Taking only 40t at t = 4 gives 160; 75 is the height at t = 3.

q: A particle has displacement s = t³ − 9t² + 24t. At the instant when its acceleration is zero, its velocity is:
x: v = 3t² − 18t + 24 and a = 6t − 18, so a = 0 at t = 3. Then v(3) = 27 − 54 + 24 = −3. 18 is s(3), the position at that moment.

q: A particle has displacement s = t³ − 6t² + 9t for t ≥ 0. Its speed is increasing exactly when:
x: v = 3(t − 1)(t − 3) and a = 6(t − 2). Speed increases when v and a have the same sign: both negative for 1 < t < 2, both positive for t > 3. Looking only at a > 0 gives t > 2.

q: A particle has displacement s = 5 + 12t − t³ metres. Its initial velocity (at t = 0) is:
x: v = ds/dt = 12 − 3t², so v(0) = 12 m/s. 5 is the initial position s(0).

q: A particle moves with constant acceleration a, starting from s = 0 with velocity u. Integrating twice, its displacement at time t is:
x: v = ∫a dt = u + at (using v(0) = u), and s = ∫(u + at) dt = ut + ½at² (using s(0) = 0). u + at is the velocity, not the displacement.

q: A stone is thrown vertically upward at 20 m/s. Take the acceleration as −10 m/s² (upward positive). After how many seconds does it return to the point of projection?
x: v = 20 − 10t gives s = 20t − 5t². s = 0 again when 5t(4 − t) = 0, so t = 4 s. 2 s is the time to the top only.

q: A particle has velocity v = 6 − 2t m/s and is at s = 1 m when t = 0. Where is it when it first comes to rest?
x: v = 0 at t = 3. s = 1 + ∫₀³ (6 − 2t) dt = 1 + (18 − 9) = 10 m. Leaving out the starting position gives 9.

q: A particle moves along a line with velocity v = 2s m/s when it is at displacement s metres. Its acceleration when s = 3 m is:
x: a = dv/dt = (dv/ds)(ds/dt) = v·dv/ds = 2s × 2 = 4s, so a = 12 m/s² at s = 3. Taking a = dv/ds = 2 forgets the chain-rule factor v; 6 is the velocity there.

q: A particle has displacement s = t² + 3t metres. Its average velocity from t = 1 s to t = 3 s is:
x: Average velocity = [s(3) − s(1)]/(3 − 1) = (18 − 4)/2 = 7 m/s. 14 forgets to divide by the time; 9 and 5 are the velocities at t = 3 and t = 1.

q: A particle starts from rest at the origin with acceleration a = 12t² m/s². Its displacement at t = 1 s is:
x: v = ∫12t² dt = 4t³ (v(0) = 0) and s = ∫4t³ dt = t⁴ (s(0) = 0), so s(1) = 1 m. 4 is the velocity at t = 1.

q: A particle has velocity v = 3t² − 12 m/s (t ≥ 0). Its acceleration at the moment it is at rest is:
x: v = 0 when t² = 4, so t = 2 (t ≥ 0). a = dv/dt = 6t = 12 m/s². Being at rest means v = 0, not a = 0.

q: For a particle moving along a line with velocity v(t), the integral of v(t) from t = t₁ to t = t₂ gives:
o: the displacement from t₁ to t₂
the total distance, even if v changes sign
x: Since v = ds/dt, ∫v dt from t₁ to t₂ = s(t₂) − s(t₁), the displacement. It equals the distance only when v keeps one sign; otherwise ∫|v| dt is needed.

q: A particle has velocity v = e^(−t) m/s. Its displacement from t = 0 to t = ln 2 s is:
x: ∫₀^(ln 2) e^(−t) dt = [−e^(−t)]₀^(ln 2) = −½ + 1 = ½ m. Using only the lower limit (e⁰ = 1) gives 1; treating ∫ as the length of the time interval gives ln 2.
